key_insight: TRIAGE improves reinforcement learning for agents by giving different kinds of actions different credit, instead of treating every action token the same. This helps the model reward useful exploration and avoid over-reinforcing redundant or harmful steps.
problem_solved: The paper addresses a core weakness in agentic reinforcement learning: standard outcome-based credit assignment gives the same advantage signal to all actions in a rollout, which can punish good exploratory actions in failed attempts and reward unnecessary actions in successful ones.
method: Introduces a role-typed credit assignment framework that distinguishes environment-facing action types such as searches, clicks, edits, navigation, and object interactions.
Uses action roles to assign more structured credit than standard GRPO’s uniform final-outcome advantage.
Targets both failed and successful rollouts so that useful exploration is preserved and regressive behavior is discouraged.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners building agents, TRIAGE offers a more precise training signal that can improve learning stability and decision quality in interactive environments. It is especially relevant for web agents, tool-using LLMs, and embodied systems where action sequences matter.

paper_title: TRIAGE: Role-Typed Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Yuanda Xu, Zhengze Zhou, Hejian Sang, Xiaomin Li, Jiaxin Zhang
